summary: Iteration 9 backend testing complete. Tested forgot/reset password flow, session management (list/revoke single/revoke others), reset-invalidates-all-sessions security guarantee, and full regression of iterations 6/7/platform-owner. Found 1 CRITICAL bug in reset-password endpoint (timezone-naive vs aware datetime comparison → 500 error) which was fixed in-place. After fix: 10/10 iter9 tests pass and 43/43 regression tests pass. Platform Owner password verified restored to NedTechOwner2026! at end of run.

critical.issue: TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes. `expires_at` is stored via `datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(hours=1)` but MongoDB returns it as naive; direct comparison with aware `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` raised 500. This meant EVERY reset-password call failed with 500 -> password never actually changed, sessions never revoked -> security guarantee broken. FIXED by me in /app/backend/app/modules/auth/routes.py (attach UTC tzinfo if naive before compare).

rca_of_the_issue: RCA: In /app/backend/app/modules/auth/routes.py::reset_password, the expires_at datetime was inserted with `datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(hours=1)` (tz-aware). MongoDB's motor driver by default returns datetimes as NAIVE (no tzinfo). The comparison `datetime.now(timezone.utc) > exp` then raised TypeError, bubbling up as HTTP 500. Reproduction: forgot-password → reset-password → 500. Mitigation applied: replaced naive datetime with UTC-aware before compare. Long-term: enable `tz_aware=True` on the motor client, OR store all timestamps as ISO strings (already the pattern for created_at/used_at).
